answer: Rotating witness quorum. Each new identity must solve a fresh challenge tied to a random vertex in the current trust graph, and the solution expires at a fixed horizon so it cannot be resold or replayed. An existing member must anchor the result by co-signing, making each identity cost one scarce attestation plus the compute to defeat time-locked puzzles. Attackers pay linear compute and a dwindling pool of honest co-signers per identity.
